en.name: John Chrysostom
en.summary: Archbishop of Constantinople and Doctor of the Church renowned for his eloquent preaching, earning him the surname "Golden-mouthed."
en.body: John trained as a monk and hermit before returning to Antioch to be ordained, where his preaching skill earned him the nickname Chrysostom, meaning golden-mouthed, and he was later summoned to become Archbishop of Constantinople in 398. There he pursued reforms of clerical excess and imperial court corruption with the same directness that had made his sermons famous, denouncing the extravagance of the Empress Eudoxia in terms pointed enough to provoke his exile, twice, the second time ending in his death from the hardships of forced travel in 407. His enormous body of preserved homilies, especially his commentaries on Scripture, remain among the most read patristic writings, and the Divine Liturgy still used in the Byzantine Rite bears his name. He is honored as one of the four great Doctors of the Eastern Church.
